b1-neoliberalismo-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Market Ideas
b1-neoliberalismo-01.scenario: You are Meg. You read a book about the 1990s in Latin America, and Carlos asks what neoliberal ideas are.
b1-neoliberalismo-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what these ideas are and what their defenders say.
cues: Say what kind of ideas they are, using a relative clause
Say what the defenders think about the market and the state
b1-neoliberalismo-01.target: Son ideas económicas que dan más importancia al mercado. Según sus defensores, el mercado asigna los recursos con más eficiencia que el Estado.
b1-neoliberalismo-01.english: They are economic ideas that give more importance to the market. According to their defenders, the market allocates resources more efficiently than the state.
b1-neoliberalismo-01.canDo: I can say what neoliberal ideas are and what their defenders argue.

b1-neoliberalismo-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What Was Sold
b1-neoliberalismo-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg watched a documentary about privatisation, and she asks what was sold in Argentina and Mexico.
b1-neoliberalismo-02.prompt: Tell Meg what was privatised in 1990 in Argentina and in Mexico.
cues: Say what happened to the telephone company in Argentina
Say what happened to Telmex in Mexico
b1-neoliberalismo-02.target: En 1990, la compañía telefónica de Argentina fue privatizada, y Telmex fue vendida a un grupo privado.
b1-neoliberalismo-02.english: In 1990, the telephone company of Argentina was privatised, and Telmex was sold to a private group.
b1-neoliberalismo-02.canDo: I can say which Argentine and Mexican companies were privatised in the 1990s.

b1-neoliberalismo-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The State Before and After
b1-neoliberalismo-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are telling Carlos what you learned in a class about the role of the state, and he asks how it changed.
b1-neoliberalismo-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the state did before the reforms and what many people thought afterwards.
cues: Say how the state protected industry
Contrast it with what many people thought after the debt crisis
b1-neoliberalismo-03.target: El Estado protegía la industria nacional con aranceles altos; sin embargo, después de la crisis de la deuda, muchos consideraron agotado ese modelo.
b1-neoliberalismo-03.english: The state protected national industry with high tariffs; however, after the debt crisis, many considered that model exhausted.
b1-neoliberalismo-03.canDo: I can describe the role of the state in the earlier model.

b1-neoliberalismo-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Growth Without Equality
b1-neoliberalismo-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg visited an exhibition about the 1990s, and she asks what improved and what did not.
b1-neoliberalismo-04.prompt: Tell Meg what improved in the 1990s and what did not.
cues: Say what grew and what fell
Say what did not fall, using a concession
b1-neoliberalismo-04.target: Aunque la economía creció y la inflación bajó, la desigualdad no bajó.
b1-neoliberalismo-04.english: Although the economy grew and inflation fell, inequality did not fall.
b1-neoliberalismo-04.canDo: I can say what many countries achieved in the 1990s and what did not improve.

b1-neoliberalismo-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Opinions
b1-neoliberalismo-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a book on the neoliberal reforms, and he asks what the two sides believe.
b1-neoliberalismo-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the defenders believe and what the critics do not believe.
cues: Say what the defenders believe about inflation
Say what the critics do not believe about the market
b1-neoliberalismo-05.target: Los defensores creen que las reformas bajaron la inflación. Los críticos no creen que el mercado pueda resolver la pobreza.
b1-neoliberalismo-05.english: The defenders believe that the reforms lowered inflation. The critics do not believe that the market can solve poverty.
b1-neoliberalismo-05.canDo: I can say what the defenders of the reforms believe.

b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Reforms in Short
b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are going over your notes before a class, and she asks you to sum up the neoliberal reforms.
b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg the term from 1989, what governments sold, and what people still discuss.
cues: Say who coined which term in 1989
Say what defenders and critics still discuss
b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.target: En 1989, John Williamson acuñó el término «Consenso de Washington». Los gobiernos vendieron empresas del Estado, y los defensores y los críticos todavía discuten si las reformas fueron un éxito.
b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.english: In 1989, John Williamson coined the term “Washington Consensus”. Governments sold state companies, and the defenders and the critics still discuss whether the reforms were a success.
b1-neoliberalismo-consolidation.canDo: I can retell the main steps of the neoliberal reforms and the debate about them.
